Bilingual Assholes Study 1: Ratings Graphs

morgan moyer

2026-06-01

Summary Stats

agr <- d %>% 
  group_by(Word) %>% 
  summarize(MeanValence = mean(likert_valence),
            V.SD = sd(likert_valence),
            MeanArousal = mean(likert_arousal),
            A.SD = sd(likert_arousal))
hist(d$likert_valence,
     # breaks = seq(0.5, 5, 9),  # centers bars on integers (for 1–7 scale)
     main = "Histogram of Likert Responses",
     xlab = "Likert Score",
     col = "lightblue")

counts <- table(d$Nativeness,d$likert_valence)

barplot(counts,
        main = "Distribution of Likert Responses",
        xlab = "Likert Score",
        ylab = "Frequency",
        col = "lightblue")

ggplot(d, aes(x = factor(likert_valence))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "lightblue") +
  facet_wrap(~Nativeness) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Likert Responses",
       x = "Likert Score",
       y = "Count")

ggplot(d, aes(x = factor(likert_arousal))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "lightblue") +
  facet_wrap(~Nativeness) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Likert Responses",
       x = "Likert Score",
       y = "Count")

names(d)
## [1] "X"              "Participant"    "Word"           "likert_arousal"
## [5] "likert_valence" "StudyLanguage"  "Nativeness"
agr <- d %>% 
  group_by(Word,Nativeness) %>% 
  summarize(MeanValence = mean(likert_valence),
            SD = sd(likert_valence),
            MeanArousal = mean(likert_arousal),
            SD = sd(likert_arousal))
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'Word'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
# dev.off()  # Close all devices
ggplot(agr, aes(x = MeanArousal, y = MeanValence, color = Nativeness)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Word), 
                  max.overlaps = Inf,
                  box.padding = 0.3,
                  point.padding = 0.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("L1" = "#F54927", "L2" = "#440E03")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 9), ylim = c(0, 9)) +  # Better than xlim/ylim
  labs(x = "Likert Arousal", y = "Likert Valence",
       # title = "Word Valence vs Arousal Ratings",
       color = "Nativeness") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12)
  )

Looking at word pairs

agr <- d %>%
  group_by(Word,Nativeness) %>% 
  summarize(MeanValence = mean(likert_valence),
            SD = sd(likert_valence),
            MeanArousal = mean(likert_arousal),
            SD = sd(likert_arousal))
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'Word'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
# View(pairs)
result <- pairs %>%
  # join English rows
  left_join(
    agr %>% filter(Nativeness == "English"),
    by = c("English" = "Word")
  ) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_EN"),
              c(MeanValence, SD, MeanArousal)) %>%
  # join Italian rows
  left_join(
    agr %>% filter(Nativeness == "Italian"),
    by = c("Italian" = "Word")
  ) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_IT"),
              c(MeanValence, SD, MeanArousal))

# result <- result %>% tidyr::drop_na()
results <- result %>% 
  mutate(MeanValDifference = abs(MeanValence_EN - MeanValence_IT),
         MeanAroDifference = abs(MeanArousal_EN - MeanArousal_IT))
names(results)
##  [1] "English"           "Italian"           "Nativeness.x"     
##  [4] "MeanValence_EN"    "SD_EN"             "MeanArousal_EN"   
##  [7] "Nativeness.y"      "MeanValence_IT"    "SD_IT"            
## [10] "MeanArousal_IT"    "MeanValDifference" "MeanAroDifference"
